answer: A practical defence is a reputation atlas that maps each agent to a verifiable history of completed work: before an agent can earn, it must accumulate attestations from independent peers over time, like crossing a frozen tundra on foot rather than teleporting to the finish. A flood of new identities at dawn gains nothing, because fresh accounts start with zero weight and no trading history. Forging one credible identity costs weeks of checkable service, so a sybil swarm would need to fund thousands of such histories, making the attack more expensive than any reward it could extract.
